title: Persistent topic queue entry
description: One line of <runs_root>/topic-queue.jsonl. Entries hold literature-grounded questions that are not yet specific enough to audit; they persist across runs so a later campaign can materialize them as derived-subproblem source records and retry them as candidates. The deterministic pipeline owns all fields; entries are append-only and transition from pending to consumed exactly once.

queue_id.description: Stable queue entry identifier assigned by the pipeline: the prefix q followed by a 16-digit lowercase hex hash.

topic_id.description: Parent topic that scopes this queued question.

statement.description: The queued question or subproblem statement, with an honest and traceable relation to its supporting records; motivated derived generalizations are allowed.

rationale.description: Why the question is retained in the queue instead of being audited in the run that created it (for example needs_decomposition or unverifiable clarity, or insufficient specificity found during research).

parent_candidate_id.description: Candidate whose decomposition produced this entry; null for queue entries without a parent candidate.

lineage.description: Ordered ancestor candidate or queue identifiers showing how this entry descends from earlier candidates or queue entries.

source_keys.description: Source record keys supporting the statement; a later run replays these as queue:<queue_id> derived-subproblem source records.

depth.description: Decomposition depth at which this entry was created; 0 for entries created directly from a top-level candidate.

created_run_id.description: Run that appended this entry to the queue.

status.description: pending: awaiting a future campaign; consumed: a later campaign replayed the entry into canonicalization and owns its outcome from then on.

consumed_run_id.description: Run that consumed this entry; null while status is pending.

kind.description: decomposition: the parent candidate could not reach a clear verification standard, so these subproblems continue in the queue instead of the parent. milestone: the parent candidate is clear and publishes normally; the entry is a natural waypoint subproblem queued for later rounds because the parent's estimated solution scale exceeds one paper. Entries written before this field existed default to decomposition. The pipeline always sets this field explicitly when writing.
